meta.description: Forms and written applications a self-represented person actually files, grouped by issue category.
meta.scope: Each entry describes the written application, where it is lodged and what is normally filed with it. It does not reproduce a State-prescribed form, because the prescribed form is set by each State and changes. Where a form number would differ by State, this file says so instead of asserting one.
meta.verificationPolicy: These are procedural descriptions, not reproduced official forms. The court or legal aid desk will give you the current prescribed form. Nothing here is a substitute for reading the form you are given.
meta.limitation: Not every category uses a form. Several proceedings begin with an oral complaint or an application on plain paper, and this file says which is which rather than implying a form always exists.

forms.name: Application for protection order and relief
forms.statute: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
forms.howToGet: Ask the Domestic Violence Cell at the Magistrate's court, or a District Legal Services Authority, for the State-prescribed form. It is also accepted as a plain written application.
whatToAttach: Proof of the marriage relationship, if any
Any medical record of injuries
Photographs or dated screenshots of threats
Names and addresses of witnesses
A short account of the incidents with dates
forms.note: All of these can be sought in one application. Asking separately costs more time and can delay the relief that matters most.

forms.name: Application for maintenance and arrears
forms.statute: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
forms.howToGet: Same court as the protection application. The State form is usually a continuation of the same application.
whatToAttach: Any earlier order of the same court
Proof of income of the respondent, if known
School records of children, for child maintenance
forms.note: Maintenance does not require you to prove abuse. The court looks at the income and the needs of the parties.

forms.name: Complaint on the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal
forms.statute: Information Technology Act, 2000 read with Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
forms.section: 66D/66E of the IT Act; s. 173 BNSS
forms.forum: Cyber Crime Cell / jurisdictional police station
forms.howToGet: File online at cybercrime.gov.in. An FIR is registered if the complaint is within the portal's reporting scope; otherwise you are given an acknowledgement and it is forwarded.
whatToAttach: Screenshot of the messages or transaction
Bank statement showing the deduction
The phone number or wallet ID used
Any transaction reference number
forms.note: Always keep the acknowledgement number. For anything involving money, file with the bank in parallel - a cyber cell complaint alone rarely reverses a transfer.

forms.name: Written complaint to the jurisdictional police station
forms.howToGet: Plain paper. No form is prescribed.
whatToAttach: Description of the property
Proof of possession such as an electricity bill or rent receipt
Any prior notice that was served
forms.note: Insist on a written receipt and note the diary number. A refusal to register an FIR can be challenged before the Superintendent of Police or a Magistrate.

forms.name: Consumer complaint
forms.forum: District / State / National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
forms.howToGet: File online at edupal.gov.in. A district commission handles claims up to the notified limit.
whatToAttach: Invoice or receipt
Warranty terms
Photographs of the defect
Any earlier complaint and its outcome
forms.note: No advocate is needed before a commission below the National Commission, and filing is by a plain written complaint.

forms.name: Written complaint to the Internal Complaints Committee
forms.statute: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
forms.forum: Internal Complaints Committee at the workplace
forms.howToGet: Ask the employer for the committee's address. The Act requires one to be constituted, so it must exist.
whatToAttach: Dates and description of the conduct
Names of witnesses
Any earlier complaint
Copies of messages, if relevant
forms.note: If the employer has not constituted a committee, that failure is itself reportable to the Local Committee. Do not wait indefinitely for an internal process that does not exist.

forms.name: Complaint to the Local Committee
forms.statute: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013
forms.forum: Local Committee at the district office
forms.howToGet: District Office of the woman and child development or the prescribed authority.
whatToAttach: The same material as the ICC complaint
Proof of employment, if you have it
forms.note: An aggrieved woman may approach the Local Committee directly. She is not required to exhaust the internal route first.

forms.name: Complaint of harassment for dowry
forms.statute: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
forms.howToGet: Same Domestic Violence Cell as any other application under the Act.
whatToAttach: Details of the demand and the amount
Any message or recording of the demand
Medical records of harm
Witnesses
forms.note: A demand made after the marriage is still dowry harassment. It need not be made before the wedding.

forms.name: Application before the Magistrate
forms.howToGet: Plain paper application at the court of the nearest Judicial Magistrate.
whatToAttach: Anything that shows the date of arrest or detention
The place of detention
A relative's affidavit
forms.note: A relative may move this. Under the D.K. Basu safeguards, the arrest memo and the Magistrate's diary entry are documents you are entitled to see.

forms.name: Legal notice for dishonour of cheque
forms.forum: Sent by post, then on complaint
forms.howToGet: No prescribed form. A written notice sent by registered post or by email and SMS is sufficient.
whatToAttach: The unpaid cheque
Bank's return memo stating the reason for dishonour
Proof of the underlying debt
forms.note: The cause of action arises from the return memo, so obtain that memo from your bank. Fifteen days from the return date is the outer limit for the complaint.

forms.name: Complaint regarding a child
forms.statute: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
forms.howToGet: Report to the police, to the Childline, or to the Special Juvenile Police Unit. A complaint may be made orally.
whatToAttach: Whatever account the child gives
Any medical examination done
Screenshots, if the conduct was online
forms.note: A child's statement may be recorded under s. 164 by the Magistrate. Request that specifically; it carries evidential weight that an informal note does not.

forms.name: Certificate for keeping a log of electronic evidence
forms.forum: Any competent authority / the court receiving the evidence
forms.howToGet: Apply for the certificate from the person who controls the device or the server on which the record is held.
whatToAttach: Identification of the device, server or email account
The period the record covers
forms.note: Electronic records need not be proved by a s. 65B certificate, but it removes any argument later that the record could have been altered. Ask for it early, because a provider may stop preserving a log once told.
